images.title: Above and below zero
images.purpose: Show that readings above 0 °C are positive and readings below 0 °C are negative.
images.composition: One tall thermometer-style scale centred, with one label on each side of the 0 mark, wide margins.
images.exact_structure: One vertical scale with 11 evenly spaced ticks from 5 at the top to −5 at the bottom, the 0 tick drawn as a longer grey #6B7280 line. A teal #0072B2 filled dot sits on the 3 tick above 0 and an amber #E69F00 filled dot sits on the −3 tick below 0; no other tick has a number. Exactly 11 ticks, 2 dots.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
numbers printed on ticks other than 0 and −3
images.takeaway: Readings above 0 °C are positive and readings below 0 °C are negative.
images.description: A vertical scale with a long line at 0 °C, a teal dot above it for a positive reading and an amber dot at −3 °C below it for a negative reading.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point above and below 0 and say which side is positive.

image_decisions.why: The sign of a temperature reading is a picture idea; one clean scale carries it.
